topic_coverage_probe.question: Is there ANY existing canonical context covering visitor identification / thumbmark, upload rate limiting or quota, AI-effect-gated uploads, or storefront upload error states?
topic_coverage_probe.answer: NO. All four topics are MISSING.
topic_coverage_probe.method: Case-insensitive full-text scan of every non-archived file under knowledge/products/teeinblue/objects/ (all 9 objects, not only the 4 hinted), plus targeted reads of every kb_candidate whose topic or statement mentioned upload / AI / effect / rate.

per_topic.topic: visitor identification / thumbmark / fingerprint / device-derived ID
per_topic.detail: 'visitor' = 0 hits anywhere. 'device info' = 0 hits. 'incognito' = 0 hits. 'fingerprint' = 1 hit, in translation/kb.json, in a parenthetical guess ('ten endpoint goi y device/browser fingerprinting, khong lien quan translation'). 'thumbmark' = 2 hits, both non-canonical asides (see OBS-CTX-05). No KB item, no profile capability, no checklist check states how a visitor is identified.
per_topic.consequence: There is nothing to regress against and nothing to contradict. Every expectation for the fixed behaviour must come from Jira, whose authority is itself qualified by task-intake ASM-01/U-01.

per_topic.topic: upload rate limiting / quota / throttle window
per_topic.detail: 'rate limit' = 2 files, both the SAME single datum (artwork KB-061 and the profile that cites it). 'quota' = 0 hits. 'throttle' = 0 hits. 'upload limit' = 0 hits. '429' = matches only a '4296 character' QR-code limit, a false positive. The one real datum (KB-061) is about response HEADERS NAMED in access-control-expose-headers on PUT /api/artworks/{id} -- a PORTAL artwork-save endpoint, not the storefront upload path -- is knowledge_kind INFERRED, confidence LOW, observed_count 1, and carries its own explicit prohibition.
per_topic.consequence: No canonical value for the window length, the default of 5, the per-visitor+per-product key, or the error response. All of those exist only in Jira comment 51220.

per_topic.topic: AI-effect-gated uploads (Remove Background / AI Enhance / Image Filter / Text-to-Image)
per_topic.verdict: MISSING as behaviour; PARTIAL as portal configuration
per_topic.detail: 'AI effect' = 0 hits; 'remove background' = 0 hits; 'AI enhance' = 0 hits. What DOES exist is portal-side config vocabulary: artwork KB-017 lists 'Image effects: Add new' as a field on the photo layer, KB-018 documents 'GenAI service*' on multiple-uploads, KB-019 documents the text-to-image layer type. Nothing anywhere states the rule 'rate limiting applies only to uploads that use an AI effect'. The closest runtime evidence is global-option KB-031 (a successful storefront text-to-image generate, 1 sample, LOW, unpublished).
per_topic.consequence: Usable to BUILD the fixture; not usable to assert what the gating rule is.

per_topic.topic: storefront upload flow and upload error states
per_topic.detail: The buyer-side upload flow is entirely unmodelled: 0 occurrences of 'upload' in sdk/features/storefront-buyer-facing/profile.json, 0 of 38 FEAT-07 checks involve uploading an image, and no error-state check exists for any upload. The only 'upload' knowledge on the storefront side is artwork KB-108/KB-093, which concern a merchant uploading an image in the PORTAL editor. sdk kb.json's own coverage_gaps list 21 declared gaps and image upload is not even named among them -- the gap is unrecognised, not merely open.
per_topic.consequence: CHECKLIST_GAP candidate at the feature level, not just the check level -- see checklist_gap_candidates below.

backend_api_object_coverage.question: Does the registry/KB have any object covering the backend/API surface (thumbmark issuance endpoint, server-side quota counter)?
backend_api_object_coverage.answer: CONFIRMED -- your reading of _registry.json is correct. It does NOT.
evidence: _registry.json lists exactly 9 objects: artwork, asset-category, campaign, font, global-option, order, product-base, sdk, translation. Every one is a portal/storefront business object; none is an API/backend/service object.
The filesystem agrees: knowledge/products/teeinblue/objects/ contains exactly those 9 folders and nothing else.

There is no object_key whose aliases include any API/backend term. The sdk aliases are all client-side ('SDK', 'storefront', 'storefront widget', 'buyer facing', 'storefront runtime', 'product page settings', 'personalization runtime', 'storefront personalization', 'add-to-cart storefront', 'password gate', 'multi-store storefront').

API knowledge exists only as APIOP-### evidence hanging off portal/storefront objects (e.g. sdk KB-013 for the public bootstrap endpoint, sdk APIOP-051 for customization save). There is no home for an endpoint that has no portal/storefront capability attached to it -- which is precisely why the thumbmark endpoint ended up in payload.unmapped_evidence in TWO different objects instead of being modelled anywhere.
The registry is also status DRAFT_NEEDS_REVIEW, i.e. the 9-object taxonomy has not been human-reviewed (task-intake U-02).
backend_api_object_coverage.consequence_for_this_task: Both server-side halves of TIB-5460's oracle -- the thumbmark issuance endpoint GET /merchant/{platform}/thumbmark and the per-visitor+per-product quota counter -- fall outside the knowledge model entirely. This is a structural coverage gap, not a stale-data problem: even a fresh Flow 1 run on the existing objects would have nowhere to put the resulting knowledge. It also means the 'Known follow-up' in comment 51220 (the thumbmark endpoint's own IP-keyed rate limit) has no canonical home either.
backend_api_object_coverage.supports_kcp: The orchestrator already raised this in task-intake object_resolution_notes. This retriever independently confirms it and recommends a KCP of proposal_type NEW_FEATURE or PROFILE_GAP against a NEW object (e.g. object_key 'api' or 'platform-api'), which only qa-context-lifecycle-orchestrator may create.

behavior_change_candidates.contradiction: The FEAT-07 page-load network baseline (campaigns/{id}.json + 2 SDK bootstrap scripts, with thumbmark relegated to unmapped_evidence) becomes materially wrong after fix part 2: thumbmark is now a deliberate, retried, 8-second-timeout page-load request, i.e. a first-class part of page-load behaviour rather than an unexplained extra.
behavior_change_candidates.strength: MODERATE. Note the tension with translation KB-017 (CTX-CONF-02), which already observed thumbmark on page load on 2026-09-21 -- that tension is unresolved and must travel with this candidate.

TIB-5460 is the first task to touch them, so the correct proposal is a NEW_FEATURE profile rather than a BEHAVIOR_CHANGE.

KB-061 concludes 'chua du evidence de ket luan co rate-limit thuc thi hay nguong bao nhieu'. TIB-5460 establishes that a real, enforced rate limit exists on the platform with concrete parameters (5 per window; 1h prod / 5min staging; keyed per visitor+product).

It should NOT be edited to adopt TIB-5460's numbers: those belong to a different endpoint.

checklist_gap_candidates.missing_case: Two distinct visitors on the same device model/region/browser build must NOT share an upload quota -- the exact collision the bug produced. No check in any checklist exercises two concurrent private sessions on one device.

A genuine repeat visitor must STILL be limited after the fix (the fix must not turn into a blanket exemption), including after a page reload within the same window -- i.e. the fallback ID must be stable per browser, not regenerated per page load. The new random-per-browser ID makes 'stable but unique' a fresh risk that no existing check covers.
checklist_gap_candidates.newly_identified_risk: Over-correction: random ID regenerated too often silently disables rate limiting.

checklist_gap_candidates.missing_case: Thumbmark fetch resilience: 8s timeout, exactly one retry on network error/5xx, and explicitly NO retry on 429. CHK-031 is the only check of its family (asserting which calls fire when) and it covers customization sync, not thumbmark; nothing anywhere covers retry policy.
checklist_gap_candidates.newly_identified_risk: A retry on 429 would amplify load against the endpoint's own IP-keyed limit -- the 'Known follow-up' in comment 51220.

checklist_gap_candidates.missing_case: localStorage teeinblue_signed_thumbmark lifecycle: written at page load, no expiry, reused on subsequent loads so no second GET fires; cleared/incognito produces a fresh fetch. CHK-023 enumerates localStorage keys but stops at the two personalization keys.
checklist_gap_candidates.newly_identified_risk: Cache behaviour is easy to mistake for a bug (comment 51220 warns testers about exactly this).

checklist_gap_candidates.missing_case: AI-effect gating: a plain upload with no AI effect must never be rate-limited, while an upload using an AI effect is. No check distinguishes the two paths; indeed no check uploads anything.
checklist_gap_candidates.newly_identified_risk: A fix to the identity path could accidentally change which uploads are counted.

checklist_gap_candidates.missing_case: CHK-005 verifies the 4 'Upload Photo' config controls but there is no check linking any of them to runtime upload behaviour, and specifically none for 'Allow buyers to choose previous processed images' (72h window) -- a per-buyer, time-windowed feature that plausibly keys off the same visitor identity this task changes.
checklist_gap_candidates.newly_identified_risk: Regression radius: changing the visitor ID could orphan a buyer's previously processed images.
